# Independent audit: maximum-volume centroid graph

Audited `candidate 7abc09359a7966ea`. Result: PASS
for its stated maximum-mass bound and equal-positive-volume consequence.

The intrinsic-dimension argument is necessary and correct: at an integer
convex-combination index, positive summand weights force the Minkowski sum
to have direction space equal to the sum of the q-dimensional direction
spaces. Maximality of q forces all of them to coincide. Only after this
step is q-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski applied. Maximality of the volume
then forces equality and actual equality of bodies, followed by translates
and centroid additivity in that proved special case.

Consequently the centroid hull has exactly one point at every nonempty
integer section, and its integer projection consists exactly of the
maximum-volume indices. For this graph the projection of G intersect A_i
is compact convex. An integer index common to those projections lifts to
one common point because the graph section is a singleton. This proves
the claimed 2^n Helly bound; it does not assume a projection/intersection
identity for arbitrary nonsingleton fibers.

The finite counting-center argument uses strict heavy-halfspace
inequalities and finite-set inward shifts to retain all closed-cap
boundary mass. The selected point is one actual maximum-fiber centroid.
Each counted centroid contributes gamma_q times its fiber volume, with
constant restrictions on its affine span giving the whole fiber. Thus
oblique cuts, lower-dimensional fibers, q=0, n=0, and d=0 all have explicit
valid treatments.

The remaining factor M_max/M is present throughout the unequal-volume
case. Its removal is not proved or implied by this audit.
